newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Kiwi International director quits - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi International director quits - NZPA.

text.p: A director of Kiwi International Airlines has quit, citing differences with the company, the New Zeealand Press Association reported on Thursday.
Mike Tournier's resignation as a director on Tuesday comes as the Hamilton-based trans-Tasman airline prepares to combat financial losses by shedding staff and services.
Kiwi's 270 staff on both sides of the Tasman will be told tonight how many jobs will be axed. The cuts will be substantial, NZPA said.
The airline's restructuring plan will be announced tomorrow.
Tournier, an air traffic control instructor, and three friends, Ewan Wilson, Mike Park and Patrick Pruett, set up the airline with $4000 two years ago.
Tournier would not elaborate on his reasons for quitting but said he would retain his shares in Kiwi, which grew out of Wilson's Hamilton travel agency as a chartered airline.
Park resigned as a director last year because of a conflict of interest: he was a pilot for Air New Zealand.
Pruett, Kiwi's managing director, this month left Hamilton for Brisbane to head the airline's operation in Queensland.
Kiwi chief executive Wilson owns 48 percent of the airline, which became a scheduled operation last August.
Wilson said on Wednesday Kiwi's restructuring was designed to claw back financial losses from a string of environmental, mechanical and timetable problems in the past two months.
Meanwhile, Hamilton airport chief executive Barry O'Connor said he was concerned that Kiwi, a major client, was having difficulties.

However he was not worried about the future of the airport, which is in the final leg of a $3 million terminal extension that was spurred on by the success of Kiwi. Further developments, including a $10 million runway extension, were on the drawing board.
O'Connor said Kiwi proved there was a good trans-Tasman market and the airport company believed the market would continue.
Kiwi's success prompted Air NZ to launch a rival regional trans-Tasman service, Freedom Air, late last year. Ansett has also since started domestic flights from the city.
